subject: Sliding versus hinged wardrobe doors
hook: Drawers behind sliding doors are the most common wardrobe planning mistake we see.
ig:
Drawers behind sliding doors are the most common wardrobe planning mistake we see.

Here is the problem. Sliding doors overlap, so at any moment part of the interior is covered by a door. Put a bank of drawers in the wrong place and it ends up straddling that overlap. You slide the door across, then find the drawer front still clips the edge of the other door.

How we plan around it:
• Drawers are sized to sit fully within one door opening
• Hanging space goes where the overlap falls, since rails do not mind
• Frequently used drawers go behind the door you open most

With hinged doors this is far less of an issue, which is one reason people who want lots of internal drawers often lean that way.

If you have already got drawers that catch, send us a photo. Planning a new fitted wardrobe? Tap the link in bio.
fb:
A small detail that makes a big difference with sliding wardrobes: where the internal drawers go.

Because sliding doors overlap, part of the wardrobe is always covered. If a set of drawers sits across that overlap, it will catch on the door every time you open it. When we design a sliding-door wardrobe, the drawers are placed so each one sits fully within a single door opening, and the hanging space goes where the doors overlap.

It is the sort of thing that is easy to get right on paper and annoying to live with if it is missed. More on our wardrobes:
